extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing reopening prosecution after appeal, supplemental examiner's answers, reply briefs, timing, dismissal, and requests for oral hearing before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening of Prosecution After Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may, with approval from the supervisory patent examiner (SPE), reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection after appellant’s brief or reply brief has been filed. The Office action containing a new ground of rejection may be made final if the new ground of rejection was (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information presented in an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) was filed. Any after-final amendment or affidavit or other evidence that was not entered before must be entered and considered on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.187 when reopening prosecution. Appellant must either (1) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (if non-final) or 1.113 (if final) or (2) initiate a new appeal under 37 CFR 41.31 followed by a brief under 41.37. Previously paid appeal fees can be applied to a new appeal; if fees increased, appellant must pay the difference. SPE approval/signature is required to reopen prosecution after an appeal. See MPEP § 706.07(a) and § 1207.04 for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Examiner's Answer Responding to a Reply Brief (No New Ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a reply brief in compliance with § 41.41, the primary examiner must acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief and may withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution or may furnish a supplemental examiner's answer responding to any new issue raised in the reply brief. A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.43(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If furnished, appellant may file another reply brief under § 41.41 within two months from the date of the supplemental examiner's answer. A Technology Center (TC) Director or designee must approve every supplemental examiner's answer. Provide examples of new issues (e.g., arguments about nonanalogous art or missing elements) that justify a supplemental answer. If a new ground is to be made, prosecution must be reopened (see MPEP § 1207.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Examiner's Answer Responding to a Board Remand for Further Consideration of a Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may provide a supplemental examiner's answer in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(a). A supplemental examiner's answer written in response to such a remand may set forth a new ground of rejection, but any new ground must comply with MPEP § 1207.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must, within two months from the mailing of the supplemental examiner’s answer, either (1) request that prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment/affidavit/evidence relevant to the remand issues (this will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal), or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41. Use form paragraph 12.185 for this supplemental answer. TC Director approval/signature is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Examiner's Answer Responding to a Board Remand for Other Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand an application for reasons other than further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider an IDS, a reply brief that raised new issues not considered earlier, an amendment, or an affidavit). The examiner may provide a supplemental examiner's answer in response to such a remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant may file a reply brief within two months of the supplemental answer. Appellant does not have the option to request that prosecution be reopened pursuant to 37 CFR 41.50(a) unless the remand is for further consideration of a rejection under 41.50(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Brief Filing Requirements and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a reply brief to an examiner's answer within two months from the date of the examiner's answer (37 CFR 41.41). A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence. A reply brief that is not in compliance with paragraph (a) will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply brief to address new grounds must include, each starting on a separate page: (A) Identification page (appellant name(s), application number, filing date, title, examiner, art unit, title of paper), (B) Status of claims page(s), (C) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal page(s), and (D) Argument page(s). A reply brief can be a substitute brief replacing the original brief but must meet 37 CFR 41.37(c) requirements. New amendments must be submitted in separate papers and their entry is governed by 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Extension Rules for Replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-month time periods for filing a reply brief or a reply to a supplemental examiner's answer are generally not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Extensions of time may be available under 37 CFR 1.136(b) for patent applications or 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For replies to supplemental examiner's answers responding to remands, if a reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, the examiner should provide a 30-day or 1 month time period (whichever is longer) for the appellant to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c). Two-month time periods are usually strict and non-extendable under 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for Failure to Timely Reply to a Supplemental Examiner's Answer on Remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to a supplemental examiner's answer that was written in response to a remand by the Board for further consideration of a rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(a), the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the rejection for which the Board remanded the proceeding. If all claims are subject, the entire appeal will be dismissed and the application may be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only some claims are subject, dismissal of the appeal as to those claims authorizes cancellation of those claims and the appeal continues as to remaining claims. The examiner must (1) cancel the claims subject to the rejection and (2) notify the appellant that the appeal as to those claims is dismissed and the claims are canceled. Use form paragraph 12.186 to dismiss and cancel claims and include appropriate bracketed insertions (dates, claim numbers). Follow MPEP § 1215 for dismissal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Acknowledgment and Response to Reply Briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply brief is filed in compliance with 37 CFR 41.41, the primary examiner must acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief. The examiner may withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution or furnish a supplemental examiner's answer responding to any new issue raised in the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply brief is not in compliance, the examiner must notify the appellant that the reply brief has not been considered and provide the reason (use form paragraph 12.182). If the reply brief has been entered and considered, use form paragraph 12.181 to acknowledge and forward the application to the Board for decision. An indication that certain rejections have been withdrawn as a result of the reply brief is not, by itself, a supplemental examiner's answer and does not give appellant the right to file another reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval Authorities for Supplemental Answers and Reopening
rubrics_metrics.description: Every supplemental examiner's answer must be approved by a Technology Center (TC) Director or designee. The examiner's decision to withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection requires approval from the supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and that approval must be indicated in the Office action setting forth the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs require insertion of TC Director or SPE signatures where indicated. TC Director/SPE approval is mandatory for supplemental answers and reopening to ensure supervisory review as required by MPEP §§ 1002.02(d), 1207.04, and 1207.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Supplemental Answers Responding to Reply Briefs (When New Ground Allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.43(a)(2) prohibits a supplemental examiner's answer responding to a reply brief from including a new ground of rejection. After the filing of a reply brief, any new ground of rejection responding to the reply brief must be by way of reopening of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of new issues that give the examiner discretion to provide a supplemental answer (but not to include a new ground) are provided (e.g., arguments that a reference is nonanalogous art or that a particular claim element is not taught). If the examiner intends to include a new ground, prosecution must be reopened with SPE approval and appropriate form language (12.187).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Briefs Required When Examiner Adds New Ground of Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner's answer contains a new ground of rejection pursuant to 37 CFR 41.39 or a supplemental examiner's answer under 37 CFR 41.50(a) contains a new ground, appellant must file a reply brief to address each new ground of rejection set forth in the answer in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vii) within two months from the mailing of the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply brief should meet brief form requirements and cannot include new or non-admitted affidavits/evidence. If the reply brief is accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence it will be treated as a request that prosecution be reopened (see 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Hearing Request and Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when appellant considers such a hearing necessary or desirable for a proper presentation of the appeal. If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months from the date of the examiner's answer or supplemental examiner's answer (37 CFR 41.47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no request and fee are timely filed, the appeal will be decided on the briefs. If a hearing is held, oral argument ordinarily is limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. At oral hearing, parties may only rely on evidence previously entered and arguments relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except upon a showing of good cause a new argument based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision may be allowed. The Board may also decline to hold a hearing even if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Reply Briefs Accompanied by Amendments or Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence (37 CFR 41.41). If a reply brief is accompanied by any amendment, affidavit or other evidence, it shall be treated as a request that prosecution be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers containing amendments are not reply briefs within the meaning of 37 CFR 41.41 and will not be entitled to entry simply by being labeled a reply brief. Entry of such amendment papers is governed by 37 CFR 41.33 and other relevant provisions. In the context of a supplemental examiner's answer under 41.50(a) written in response to a remand for further consideration, any reply brief accompanied by amendment, affidavit, or other evidence will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution before the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Prescribed Form Paragraphs and Required Insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use the prescribed form paragraphs (e.g., ¶12.187, ¶12.184, ¶12.185, ¶12.186, ¶12.182, ¶12.181) when preparing office actions associated with reopening prosecution, supplemental examiner's answers, dismissals, acknowledgments, and notices regarding reply briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph bracket fields must be filled per Examiner Notes (e.g., dates, claim numbers, reasons, whether 'A new ground of rejection is' or 'New grounds of rejection are', and signatures of SPE or TC Director). Use the specified paragraphs for the corresponding procedural situation to ensure correctness and consistency with MPEP guidance.
